items.title: fix(sync-models): validate opencode.jsonc shape at the parse boundary (#2832)
items.body: Fixes #2832. Design #3068 Phase 2 (parsed files in tools) for sync-models. ## Problem A parseable-but-wrong-shaped `opencode.jsonc` (`"google": "oops"`, `"models": "oops"`, an array provider entry, or no `provider` key at all) crashed sync-models with raw TypeErrors naming neither the file nor the key — in `run()`'s provider derefs and in the JSONC tree editor's `members` walks — blocking sync for every provider until a human guessed the bad key. ## Changes (bin/sync-models.mjs) - **`validateConfigShape(config, configPath)`** runs immediately after `parseJsonc` in `run()`, in the same clean-exit path as a parse error: root, `provider`, each provider entry, and each `models` container must be plain objects, otherwise one named error — `invalid config shape in : provider.google: expected object, got string`. Whole-job refusal with a diagnostic, per the #3068 Phase 2 leaning recorded for #2832. - **Missing `provider` key = nothing to sync**, not a crash: the two remaining `config.provider` derefs (antigravity block, openai sync) now use optional chaining. - **Tree editor guards:** `setJsoncPath` / `removeJsoncPath` refuse a non-object intermediate node with an error naming the full key path and the offending prefix, instead of dereferencing `members` on a scalar/array node. ## Tests (bin/sync-models.test.mjs) New #2832 tests pin: scalar provider entry, array provider entry, scalar `models`, wrong-shaped `provider` container and root, missing `provider` key (no throw), well-formed config (no throw), tree-editor refusal for scalar/array intermediates, and the well-formed set control. Laptop run: `node --test bin/sync-models.test.mjs` — 35 pass, 0 fail (all pre-existing tests stay green). Oracle: the named-error messages above; before this change the same shapes threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'find')` / `Cannot create property … on string 'oops'`. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: Update Rust crate sqlx to 0.8.0 [SECURITY]
items.body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [sqlx](https://redirect.github.com/launchbadge/sqlx) | dependencies | minor | `0.7.1` → `0.8.0` |

---

### SQLx Binary Protocol Misinterpretation caused by Truncating or Overflowing Casts
[GHSA-xmrp-424f-vfpx](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmrp-424f-vfpx)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
The following presentation at this year's DEF CON was brought to our attention on the SQLx Discord:

> SQL Injection isn't Dead: Smuggling Queries at the Protocol Level  
> <http://web.archive.org/web/20240812130923/https://media.defcon.org/DEF%20CON%2032/DEF%20CON%2032%20presentations/DEF%20CON%2032%20-%20Paul%20Gerste%20-%20SQL%20Injection%20Isn't%20Dead%20Smuggling%20Queries%20at%20the%20Protocol%20Level.pdf>  
> (Archive link for posterity.)

Essentially, encoding a value larger than 4GiB can cause the length prefix in the protocol to overflow, 
causing the server to interpret the rest of the string as binary protocol commands or other data.

It appears SQLx _does_ perform truncating casts in a way that could be problematic, 
for example: <https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/blob/6f2905695b9606b5f51b40ce10af63ac9e696bb8/sqlx-postgres/src/arguments.rs#L163>

This code has existed essentially since the beginning, 
so it is reasonable to assume that all published versions `<= 0.8.0` are affected.

##### Mitigation

As always, you should make sure your application is validating untrustworthy user input. 
Reject any input over 4 GiB, or any input that could _encode_ to a string longer than 4 GiB. 
Dynamically built queries are also potentially problematic if it pushes the message size over this 4 GiB bound.

[`Encode::size_hint()`](https://docs.rs/sqlx/latest/sqlx/trait.Encode.html#method.size_hint) 
can be used for sanity checks, but do not assume that the size returned is accurate. 
For example, the `Json<T>` and `Text<T>` adapters have no reasonable way to predict or estimate the final encoded size, 
so they just return `size_of::<T>()` instead.

For web application backends, consider adding some middleware that limits the size of request bodies by default.

##### Resolution

Work has started on a branch to add `#[deny]` directives for the following Clippy lints:

* [`cast_possible_truncation`](https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/#/cast_possible_truncation)
* [`cast_possible_wrap`](https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/#/cast_possible_wrap)
* [`cast_sign_loss`](https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/#/cast_sign_loss)

and to manually audit the code that they flag.

A fix is expected to be included in the `0.8.1` release (still WIP as of writing).

#### Severity
Medium

#### References
- [https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/issues/3440](https://redirect.github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/issues/3440)
- [https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/blob/6f2905695b9606b5f51b40ce10af63ac9e696bb8/sqlx-postgres/src/arguments.rs#L163](https://redirect.github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/blob/6f2905695b9606b5f51b40ce10af63ac9e696bb8/sqlx-postgres/src/arguments.rs#L163)
- [https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0363.html](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0363.html)
- [https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmrp-424f-vfpx](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmrp-424f-vfpx)

This data is provided by the [GitHub Advisory Database](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmrp-424f-vfpx) ([CC-BY 4.0](https://redirect.github.com/github/advisory-database/blob/main/LICENSE.md)).
</details>

---

Postgres users are advised to upgrade ASAP as a possible exploit has been demonstrated:
[#​3440 (comment)](https://redirect.github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/issues/3440#issuecomment-2307956901)

MySQL and SQLite do not *appear* to be exploitable, but upgrading is recommended nonetheless.

##### Breaking

- \[[#​2697]]: fix(macros): only enable chrono when time is disabled \[\[[@​saiintbrisson](https://redirect.github.com/saiintbrisson)]]

  - Potentially breaking: nullability inference changes for SQLite.

  - Potentially breaking: attributes on `#[sqlx::test]` usages are applied in the correct order now.

  - Breaking changes to `MigrateError`.
- \[[#​3181]]: feat: no tx migration \[\[[@​cleverjam](https://redirect.github.com/cleverjam)]]
  - (Postgres only) migrations that should not run in a transaction can be flagged by adding `-- no-transaction` to the beginning.
  - Breaking change: added field to `Migration`
- \[[#​3184]]: \[BREAKING} fix(sqlite): always use `i64` as intermediate when decoding \[\[[@​abonander](https://redirect.github.com/abonander)]]
  - integer decoding will now loudly error on overflow instead of silently truncating.
  - some usages of the query!() macros might change an i32 to an i64.
- \[[#​3252]]: fix `#[derive(sqlx::Type)]` in Postgres \[\[[@​abonander](https://redirect.github.com/abonander)]]
  - Manual implementations of PgHasArrayType for enums will conflict with the generated one. Delete the manual impl or add `#[sqlx(no_pg_array)]` where conflicts occur.
  - Type equality for PgTypeInfo is now schema-aware.
- \[[#​3329]]: fix: correct handling of arrays of custom types in Postgres \[\[[@​abonander](https://redirect.github.com/abonander)]]
  - Potential breaking change: `PgTypeInfo::with_name()` infers types that start with `_` to be arrays of the un-prefixed type. Wrap type names in quotes to bypass this behavior.
- \[[#​3356]]: breaking: fix name collision in `FromRow`, return `Error::ColumnDecode` for `TryFrom` errors \[\[[@​abonander](https://redirect.github.com/abonander)]]
  - Breaking behavior change: errors with `#[sqlx(try_from = "T")]` now return `Error::ColumnDecode` instead of `Error::ColumnNotFound`.
  - Breaking because `#[sqlx(default)]` on an individual field or the struct itself would have previously suppressed the error.
    This doesn't seem like good behavior as it could result in some potentially very difficult bugs.
    - Instead, create a wrapper implementing `From` and apply the default explicitly.
- \[[#​3337]]: allow rename with rename_all (close [#​2896](https://redirect.github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/issues/2896)) \[\[[@​DirectorX](https://redirect.github.com/DirectorX)]]
  - Changes the precedence of `#[sqlx(rename)]` and `#[sqlx(rename_all)]` to match the expected behavior (`rename` wins).

This is officially the **last** release of the 0.7.x release cycle.

As of this release, development of 0.8.0 has begun on `main` and only high-priority bugfixes may be backported.

##### Added

- \[[#​2891]]: feat: expose getters for connect options fields \[\[[@​saiintbrisson](https://redirect.github.com/saiintbrisson)]]
- \[[#​2902]]: feat: add `to_url_lossy` to connect options \[\[[@​lily-mosquitoes](https://redirect.github.com/lily-mosquitoes)]]
- \[[#​2927]]: Support `query!` for cargo-free systems \[\[[@​kshramt](https://redirect.github.com/kshramt)]]
- \[[#​2997]]: doc(FAQ): add entry explaining prepared statements \[\[[@​abonander](https://redirect.github.com/abonander)]]
- \[[#​3001]]: Update README to clarify MariaDB support \[\[[@​iangilfillan](https://redirect.github.com/iangilfillan)]]
- \[[#​3004]]: feat(logging): Add numeric elapsed time field elapsed_secs \[\[[@​iamjpotts](https://redirect.github.com/iamjpotts)]]
- \[[#​3007]]: feat: add `raw_sql` API \[\[[@​abonander](https://redirect.github.com/abonander)]]
  - This hopefully makes it easier to find how to execute statements which are not supported by the default
    prepared statement interfaces `query*()` and `query!()`.
  - Improved documentation across the board for the `query*()` functions.
  - Deprecated: `execute_many()` and `fetch_many()` on interfaces that use prepared statements.
    - Multiple SQL statements in one query string were only supported by SQLite because its prepared statement
      interface is the *only* way to execute SQL. All other database flavors forbid multiple statements in
      one prepared statement string as an extra defense against SQL injection.
    - The new `raw_sql` API retains this functionality because it explicitly does *not* use prepared statements.
      Raw or text-mode query interfaces generally allow multiple statements in one query string, and this is
      supported by all current databases. Due to their nature, however, one cannot use bind parameters with them.
    - If this change affects you, an issue is open for discussion: [#​3108](https://redirect.github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/issues/3108)
- \[[#​3011]]: Added support to IpAddr with MySQL/MariaDB. \[\[[@​Icerath](https://redirect.github.com/Icerath)]]

items.title: feat(openclaw): opencode-route provider proxy — OpenCode server front for OpenClaw (#2229)
items.body: Method 3 of code#2229: an OpenAI-compatible front so OpenClaw can run jobs carried by the OpenCode workhorse route. ## What - **bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs** (new): chat-completions facade on fixed port **18750** (next free in the #437 block), mirroring the commandcode proxy pattern. Each request creates one session on the laptop OpenCode server via its v2 API (`POST /api/session` with `model:{providerID:"opencode-route", id:}`), prompts it, waits for settle, and returns the assistant text as a chat completion. Streaming supported via message polling. OpenAI tool_calls are not round-tripped — the OpenCode build agent executes with its own tools server-side (documented in the file header). - **bin/opencode-route-proxy-start.sh** + **bin/opencode-route-proxy.test.mjs** (new; tests pass 2/2). - **home/common/default.nix**: `opencodeRouteProxyPort = 18750`, proxy-supervisor entry, manual-fallback systemd unit (no Install.WantedBy — the supervisor owns the process, per the 2026-10-26 commandcode lesson). - **home/openclaw/default.nix**: `models.providers.opencode-route` (workhorse, speed, specialist, summit, scout), gateway After/Wants on the proxy unit, laptop-operations port list updated. ## Live proof (2026-10-29, from this worktree) - `POST /v1/chat/completions {model:"opencode-route/workhorse"}` → `ROUTE-PROXY-OK`. - `openclaw agent --local --model opencode-route/workhorse` → replied **OC-ROUTE-OK**; run meta: provider `opencode-route`, model `workhorse`, fallbackUsed=false. - Verified in the OpenCode v2 tables: session **ses_e5e78b6f4f4ffeVyPSZquFZkwV** ("opencode-route-proxy: workhorse"), assistant carried by providerID `opencode-go`, model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, variant `high` — the workhorse pool door. Deploys permanently at the next switch (supervisor takes over port 18750 from the checkout). --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint for health checks, model listings, and chat completions. * Added five selectable OpenCode models: Workhorse, Speed, Specialist, Summit, and Scout. * Chat completions support both streaming and non-streaming responses, with usage information included for streaming. * The service restarts automatically if it stops, and completion requests have a configurable timeout. * **Bug Fixes** * Invalid or empty requests and unavailable upstream services now return clear error responses.
